- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 30d horizon.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 30d horizon.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 7d high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or adjust downward by 2–4% for next 7d.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 70+ to 60–65), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 14d.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1–2 positive, 1–2 negative), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.  
- For 30d horizon, if model consistently forecasts >70% above recent 18d mean, reduce by 3–5% to align with observed downward drift.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by 1–2% downward for next 7d.
